title: Add invocation-skeleton metrics and log-context bridging for long-tail investigations
author: Ethan Caldwell
release_notes: Introduce invocation-skeleton telemetry (timing anchors + exemplar linking) and a log-context bridge for targeted long-tail investigation. Adds UI panels and alert tuning. Disabled by default via feature flag; opt-in rollout for Hosted/Dedicated/Private.
description: Context: we need lower-noise, high-signal artifacts to investigate long-tail cost/latency incidents that span gateway/router/runtime/kv-cache boundaries. This PR adds an 'invocation-skeleton' telemetry record that captures stage timing anchors, per-stage resource tags, and a compact exemplar id that can be used to join logs and traces across subsystems. Design: 1) A lightweight telemetry packet emitted at request completion with stage timings (gateway_enter,gateway_exit,router_dispatch,runtime_start,runtime_end,kv_cache_hit) and derived metrics (token_cost_estimate,peak_gpu_mem_mb). 2) Exemplar linking: each sampled skeleton gets a stable exemplar_id (hex64) propagated to logs and attached to the trace/span as 'exemplar.id' for fast join. 3) Adaptive sampling profiles: sampling is weighted by token-cost, stage skew, and historical anomaly score so we increase sampling on long-tail/expensive invocations while keeping overall telemetry volume bounded. 4) Log-context bridge service: a tiny indexer service that maps exemplar_id -> log pointers (s3 shard + byte offset or kinesis seq) to enable fast retrieval without scanning whole log sets. Implementation notes: all skeleton emission is behind a runtime feature flag 'obs.invocation_skeleton' default false. Emitted records are protobuf-encoded, compressed with snappy, and pushed to the existing observability ingestion pipeline with a new schema version. The exemplar index is appended to a compact key-value store (small write QPS) with TTL; the bridge exposes a one-shot fetch API used by Console. Dashboards: new dashboard 'Invocation Skeletons' under Observability with panels showing skeleton latency cohort histograms, stage skew distribution, exemplar-linked tail explorer, and token-cost vs stage-duration scatter. Alerting: new aggregate SLI 'skeleton_long_tail_rate' and tuned alert runbooks that only page when cohort-level p99 delta exceeds baseline and exemplar density is > threshold. Rollout plan: canary 10% of requests (runtime flag) for 48h, expand to 50% for 72h with extra traces sampled, then cluster-wide enable. For Dedicated/Private, runtime package includes installer toggle documented in private-installer/README. Backwards compatibility: ingestion understands old schema and drops skeleton records when flag is off. Tests & CI: unit tests for serializer, integration tests exercising indexer reads and the Console exemplar viewer, perf bench that shows median latency <0.2% overhead and p99 <0.7% overhead at 99th percentile with sampling at configured rates. Migration: small KV schema migration to add exemplar index table; migration is additive and non-blocking. Observability cost: estimated +0.6% ingestion cost at canary sample rates, tuned down after initial profiling. Security: exemplar ids are random and non-identifying; no PII is added. Docs: Console docs and internal runbook updated. Why unique: this approach provides a compact, structured artifact purpose-built for joins across logs/traces/metrics enabling engineers to investigate tail events without turning on full request-level tracing or increasing trace sampling dramatically.

notes_for_ops: Feature flag obs.invocation_skeleton must be enabled on runtime nodes. Indexer needs a small KV table and 1 replica by default. Monitor ingestion queue depth and exemplar index write latency. Rollback by disabling feature flag and draining indexer writes.
how_to_validate: 1) Enable flag for canary hosts and generate synthetic high-token requests. 2) Verify skeleton records appear in ingestion with stage timings and exemplar.id. 3) Use Console > Invocation Skeletons > Exemplar Viewer to retrieve log fragments. 4) Validate adaptive sampling increases exemplar density for expensive invocations. 5) Confirm no PII present in skeleton payloads.
